### GEMINI
The output of your cat /etc/resolv.conf command shows that your WSL2 instance is not using the 8.8.8.8 DNS server we set in .wslconfig. Instead, it's using 10.255.255.254, which is likely a local DNS server provided by your router or network. This means the .wslconfig change you made didn't take effect, or something else is overriding it. This is why you're still facing NameResolutionError for superboogav2. Fixing the Persistent DNS Issue Since .wslconfig didn't work as expected, we need to try an alternative method to force WSL2 to use a reliable DNS server. We'll disable the automatic resolv.conf generation within WSL2 itself and then manually set the DNS. Here's how to do it: Step 1: Prevent Automatic resolv.conf Generation Close all WSL2 terminals. Open PowerShell or Command Prompt (on Windows) as Administrator. Run: wsl --shutdown Open a new WSL2 terminal. Create or edit the wsl.conf file: This file controls WSL2's internal settings. sudo nano /etc/wsl.conf If the file is empty or doesn't exist, simply add the following content. If it already has content, add this new section: [network] generateResolvConf = false This tells WSL2 not to automatically create/overwrite /etc/resolv.conf on startup. Save the file: Press Ctrl+O, then Enter, then Ctrl+X. Step 2: Manually Configure DNS in /etc/resolv.conf Now that WSL2 won't overwrite it, we can set the DNS server manually. Close all WSL2 terminals again. Open PowerShell or Command Prompt (on Windows) as Administrator. Run: wsl --shutdown Open a new WSL2 terminal. Edit the resolv.conf file: sudo nano /etc/resolv.conf Delete all existing lines in this file. Add the following lines: nameserver 8.8.8.8 You can also add nameserver 8.8.4.4 below it as a backup, or use Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 and 1.0.0.1. For now, 8.8.8.8 is sufficient to test. Save the file: Press Ctrl+O, then Enter, then Ctrl+X. Verify the change (optional): cat /etc/resolv.conf It should now show nameserver 8.8.8.8. Step 3: Clear Hugging Face Cache and Restart Oobabooga Since the DNS wasn't working, the previous cache deletion might not have fully prevented the re-download attempt. Ensure you have an active internet connection. Stop Oobabooga (Ctrl+C if running). Navigate to the Hugging Face cache directory: cd ~/.cache/huggingface/hub Delete the specific model cache again: rm -rf models--sentence-transformers--all-MiniLM-L6-v2 Go back to your Oobabooga directory: cd ~/text-generation-webui/ Run Oobabooga: ./installer_files/env/bin/python server.py This sequence should force WSL2 to use 8.8.8.8 for DNS, allowing superboogav2 to successfully download and cache its embedding model. Once that's done, it should load offline without errors on subsequent boots (as long as web_rag is off).
